messages:
maria: Quick question — where do folks usually look for traces/logs when we see transient high SM%? Trying to correlate smem spikes with KV cache evictions and recent batch-size tweaks. Any dashboard or Jaeger link?

ashok: Grafana: gpu -> 'Throughput & SM' has SM% by host. Also check the 'KV cache' panels on the same dashboard for evictions.

ashok: Jaeger service name is `runtime-inference`. Filter spans by `serve-token` and add tag `gpu_host`.

maria: can you drop a link? saves me hunting. :pray:

ashok: sure — gpu dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/gpu-throughput/throughput-sm-kv?orgId=1

ashok: jaeger: https://jaeger.redwood.company/search?service=runtime-inference&span=serve-token

oliver: quick logs query (loki) that helped me spot evictions:
```
{cluster=\"prod\"} | json | sm_util>80 and kvcache_evictions>0 | sort_desc timestamp
```

maria: perfect, thanks. For the alerting side — our canary alert is firing at 85% smem. That’s noisy during peak batch tests. Should we raise it for canary only?

kevin: yes, canary should be more forgiving. I can open a small PR to bump canary threshold to 88% and leave global at 85%.

jess: please add an annotation in the alert with a link to the grafana + jaeger so oncall can triage faster.

kevin: will do. cc @runtime-bot to add runbook link in alert policy.

runtime-bot: runbook available — https://docs.redwood.company/runbooks/gpu-smem-kvcache. Recommend: add annotation `runbook: true`.

maria: awesome. last ask — if you tweak the threshold, can you also add a note in the PR describing expected false positive window? we had a morning spike last week during nightly eval.

kevin: yep, PR coming in ~30m. I'll include observed spike timestamps and a link to the trace I found.

jess: thanks — once PR is merged, I'll update the rollout checklist so PMs know the canary change. :thumbsup:

maria: great, this helps a lot. If anyone sees a reproduction recipe for the batch-size-induced smem jump, please paste it here.

oliver: posting short repro in eng-runtime thread in a bit.

maria: thanks all! :rocket:
